title: Appendiceal Neoplasms & Cancers
subtitle: LAMN / HAMN (Pseudomyxoma Peritonei) and Adenocarcinoma / Goblet Cell Pathways
provenanceNote: Clinical algorithms extracted from NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 for Appendiceal Neoplasms and Cancers.
sourceNote: NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 - Appendiceal Neoplasms and Cancers (APP-1 to APP-9, APP-A to APP-E)

footnotes.fn_pmp: Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) +/- HIPEC should be performed at specialized peritoneal surface oncology centers.
footnotes.fn_gca: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma requires oncologic right hemicolectomy and behaves like aggressive adenocarcinoma.

nodes.name: Clinical Presentation
nodes.title: Appendiceal Neoplasm: Clinical Presentation & Diagnostic Suspicion
nodes.description: Incidental finding on appendectomy, acute appendicitis presentation, palpable abdominal mass, or new mucinous ascites / pseudomyxoma peritonei.
bullets: Clinical presentation: incidental finding during appendectomy for acute appendicitis (~1-2% of appendectomies), unexplained right lower quadrant mass, new ovarian mass (Krukenberg tumor), or mucinous ascites (pseudomyxoma peritonei).
Operative note review: meticulously examine operative reports from prior surgery for signs of gross rupture/perforation, presence of intraperitoneal mucin, or serosal implants.

options.label: Suspicion / confirmation of appendiceal neoplasm - Proceed to workup

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Appendiceal Neoplasms: Mandatory Staging & Laboratory Checklist
nodes.description: High-resolution cross-sectional staging, serum tumor marker panel, and colonoscopy.
bullets: Staging Imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis (C/A/P) with oral and IV contrast. Non-contrast chest CT + abdominal/pelvic MRI is preferred if iodinated contrast is contraindicated.

FDG-PET/CT is generally NOT indicated: Low-grade mucinous tumors have minimal FDG uptake and high false-negative rates; reserve PET/CT only for equivocal CT findings in high-grade non-mucinous adenocarcinomas.

Serum Tumor Marker Triad: Mandatory baseline measurement of Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA), Carbohydrate Antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9), and Cancer Antigen 125 (CA-125; particularly elevated in women with peritoneal/ovarian involvement).
Screening Colonoscopy: Mandatory for all confirmed appendiceal neoplasms to rule out synchronous colorectal adenomas or adenocarcinomas prior to definitive surgical therapy.

DPYD Testing (NCCN / FDA Boxed Warning): Pre-treatment testing for DPYD gene variants (*2A, *13, c.2846A>T, HapB3) recommended prior to initiating fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy (5-FU or capecitabine).
Molecular Profiling: Mandatory testing for MMR/MSI status, KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF V600E mutations in advanced/metastatic disease.

nodes.name: Histopathology Subtype
nodes.title: Appendiceal Neoplasm: Histopathologic Classification
nodes.description: Pathology review by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist distinguishes mucinous neoplasms from invasive adenocarcinoma and goblet cell adenocarcinoma.
bullets: Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm (LAMN): Villous/flat proliferation of low-grade mucinous epithelium with pushing borders, attenuation of muscularis, and potential to shed mucin causing pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP).
High-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm (HAMN): Cytologic high-grade atypia in a mucinous neoplasm with pushing invasion (no infiltrative invasion).
Appendiceal Adenocarcinoma (AA): Infiltrative glandular proliferation (mucinous or non-mucinous / signet ring cell) with desmoplastic stroma and high risk of lymph node metastasis.
Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma (GCA): Amphicrine neoplasm composed of clusters of mucin-filled goblet-like cells with neuroendocrine features; aggressive behavior requiring oncologic colectomy.

options.label: Invasive Cancer: Appendiceal Adenocarcinoma (AA) or Goblet Cell (GCA)

nodes.name: LAMN/HAMN Extent
nodes.title: LAMN / HAMN: Staging & Extraperitoneal / Peritoneal Extent
nodes.description: Assess whether mucinous disease is confined to appendix or has caused peritoneal mucinous seeding (pseudomyxoma peritonei).
bullets: Appendix-only: Confined to the appendix with clear surgical resection margins, no perforation, and no extra-appendiceal mucin or cells.
Peritoneal-only: Disseminated peritoneal mucin or mucinous deposits (pseudomyxoma peritonei, PMP), without hematogenous or parenchymal metastasis.

options.label: Confined to Appendix (Negative margins, no peritoneal mucin)
Peritoneal-Only Disease (Pseudomyxoma Peritonei / Mucin in Peritoneum)

nodes.name: Localized LAMN/HAMN Tx
nodes.title: Localized LAMN / HAMN: Surgical Margins & Long-Term Surveillance
nodes.description: Complete surgical resection without lymphadenectomy, followed by long-term surveillance.
bullets: Resection Margin Assessment:

• Negative appendiceal base margin: Simple appendectomy is completely curative. Routine right hemicolectomy is NOT indicated (LAMN does not spread via lymphatics in the absence of invasive carcinoma).
• Positive margin at appendiceal base: Partial cecectomy or cecal wedge resection to achieve an R0 negative margin.
No adjuvant chemotherapy: Cytotoxic chemotherapy has no proven role in localized LAMN/HAMN.
Surveillance Protocol (Long-term 10-year follow-up):
• H&P and tumor markers (CEA, CA 19-9, CA-125) every 6-12 months for 2 years, then annually for up to 10 years.
• Abdominal/pelvic CT or MRI with contrast every 6-12 months for 2 years, then every 12-24 months for up to 10 years (delayed peritoneal recurrences can occur up to a decade later).

nodes.name: PMP Cytoreduction (CRS)
nodes.title: Peritoneal LAMN/HAMN (Pseudomyxoma Peritonei): CRS +/- HIPEC
nodes.description: Multidisciplinary management at high-volume peritoneal surface malignancy center.
bullets: Multidisciplinary evaluation at an experienced peritoneal surface oncology center.
Cytoreductive Surgery (CRS) with intent of complete gross resection:

• Peritonectomy procedures and visceral resections (greater omentectomy, right hemicolectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in women, pelvic peritonectomy, stripping of diaphragmatic peritoneum) to achieve Completeness of Cytoreduction score CC-0 (no visible residual) or CC-1 (residual nodules <2.5 mm).
Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC):
• Intraperitoneal perfusion with heated Mitomycin C (41-43°C x 60-90 minutes) or Oxaliplatin upon completion of cytoreduction.
Unresectable / Debilitated Patients: Serial debulking for symptom relief, or observation for asymptomatic indolent acellular mucin deposits.
Post-CRS Surveillance: Follow-up CT A/P and tumor marker panel every 6 months for 2 years, then annually for up to 10 years.

nodes.name: AA/GCA Clinical Extent
nodes.title: Appendiceal Adenocarcinoma (AA) / Goblet Cell (GCA): Staging
nodes.description: Delineate localized, peritoneal-only, or systemic extraperitoneal metastatic disease.
bullets: Localized Disease: Confined to appendix and regional mesentery without peritoneal seeding or distant metastasis.
Peritoneal-Only Metastases: Peritoneal carcinomatosis / deposits without extraperitoneal visceral involvement.
Extraperitoneal Metastatic Disease: Liver metastases (within parenchyma), distant retroperitoneal nodes, or lung/pleural metastases.

options.label: Extraperitoneal Metastatic Disease (Liver Parenchyma, Lung, Distant)

nodes.name: AA/GCA Resection & Adjuvant
nodes.title: Localized AA / GCA: Right Hemicolectomy & Risk-Adapted Adjuvant Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Oncologic right hemicolectomy followed by colorectal-aligned adjuvant systemic chemotherapy.
bullets: Definitive Surgical Resection: Right hemicolectomy with ileocolic lymphadenectomy (examination of >=12 lymph nodes is mandatory for accurate pathological staging). In women, bilateral oophorectomy should be strongly considered (high rate of synchronous/metachronous ovarian involvement).
Pathologic Staging & Adjuvant Chemotherapy Decision (Colorectal-extrapolated guidelines):
• Stage I (pT1-2 N0 M0): Observation; adjuvant chemotherapy not indicated.
• Stage II (pT3-4 N0 M0) High-Risk (perforated primary, T4, poorly differentiated/signet ring, <12 nodes examined) or Stage III (pN+ M0): Adjuvant systemic chemotherapy for 3 to 6 months.
Preferred Adjuvant Regimens (modified-folfox-6):
• Modified FOLFOX6 (modified-folfox-6): Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU bolus + 46-h continuous infusion q14d.
• CAPOX: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 PO BID x 14d + Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 q21d.
Surveillance: H&P, C/A/P CT with contrast, and CEA/CA 19-9/CA-125 every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6 months for a total of 5 years.

nodes.name: Peritoneal AA/GCA Therapy
nodes.title: Peritoneal AA / GCA: Systemic Chemotherapy +/- Cytoreductive Surgery (CRS)
nodes.description: Perioperative systemic chemotherapy and cytoreduction at specialized peritoneal malignancy center.
bullets: Multidisciplinary tumor board at specialized peritoneal center.
Neoadjuvant / Induction Systemic Chemotherapy (2-4 months):
• Modified FOLFOX6 (modified-folfox-6) or CAPOX (+/- Bevacizumab) to assess tumor biology and achieve disease stability before major cytoreduction.
Cytoreductive Surgery (CRS) + HIPEC consideration:
• In patients with responsive or stable disease and low-to-moderate Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) amenable to complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), complete CRS +/- HIPEC significantly improves survival.
Postoperative Systemic Chemotherapy: Complete remaining cycles of systemic therapy to achieve 6 months total perioperative duration.
Unresectable Peritoneal Disease: Continued systemic chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6, FOLFIRI, or FOLFOXIRI +/- bevacizumab); palliative surgical bypass or stenting as needed for bowel obstruction.

nodes.name: Extraperitoneal Metastatic Tx
nodes.title: Extraperitoneal Metastatic AA / GCA: Systemic Chemotherapy & Targeted Biologics
nodes.description: Systemic palliative therapy for parenchymal liver, lung, or distant nodal metastases.
bullets: First-Line Systemic Chemotherapy:
• Modified FOLFOX6 (modified-folfox-6) or CAPOX combined with Bevacizumab (5 mg/kg q2w or 7.5 mg/kg q3w).
• FOLFIRI (folfiri) + Bevacizumab: Preferred second-line or alternative first-line.
Biomarker-Directed Targeted Options:
• MSI-H / dMMR: Pembrolizumab or Dostarlimab (preferred first-line or subsequent therapy).
• KRAS/NRAS/BRAF wild-type: Consider Anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody (Cetuximab or Panitumumab) in later lines.
Oligometastatic Disease: In patients with solitary liver or lung metastasis achieving durable response to chemotherapy, surgical resection or thermal ablation can be considered.
Palliative & Best Supportive Care: Early involvement of palliative care team for symptom management, pain control, and nutritional support.
